title: Pujara Backs Kohli for Hundred, Predicts 2-2 Draw in New Zealand ODIs
excerpt: Speaking on JioStar, Cheteshwar Pujara says Kohli's No. 3 anchor role gives him the edge over Rohit Sharma, and India's split squad points to a drawn series.
body:
• Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara, speaking on JioStar, says Virat Kohli has slightly better chances than Rohit Sharma of scoring a hundred in the New Zealand ODI series because his No. 3 anchor role suits building a century.
  • Pujara predicts a 2-2 result in the five-match series, which runs November 4 to 15, 2026, citing India's split squad and the chance of a rain washout.
  • Both batters arrive in form from the West Indies series: Kohli made 168 runs in three innings, Rohit 225 at an average of 75.00, according to CricTracker.

Cheteshwar Pujara has backed Virat Kohli to score a hundred in India's ODI series in New Zealand, and predicted the five-match series will finish 2-2. The former India batter, speaking on JioStar, said Kohli's position at No. 3 gives him a slightly better chance of reaching three figures than opener Rohit Sharma, whose powerplay role may change in New Zealand conditions. CricTracker reports the series runs from November 4 to November 15, 2026, across Auckland, Mount Maunganui, Hamilton and Wellington.

"For Virat, the chances are slightly higher because he bats at number three. His game is more about playing the anchor role."

— Cheteshwar Pujara, on JioStar

The reasoning: anchor versus powerplay

Pujara's argument is about roles, not form. Rohit, he said, has a role of providing good starts in the powerplay, and in New Zealand that role may change, so Rohit could also go on to a century. Kohli's game, by contrast, is built around anchoring an innings from No. 3, which Pujara said makes scoring a century in the ODI format a bit easier. The opener's role is defined, he added, but in New Zealand conditions that changes a bit, which is why he feels Kohli has more chances of scoring a hundred there than Rohit.

Both men arrive with runs behind them. CricTracker reports Kohli accumulated 168 runs across three innings against West Indies, highlighted by an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls while chasing 296 in the opening match. Rohit amassed 225 runs in three innings against the same opposition at an average of 75.00, registering a century and a highest score of 101 at a strike rate above 115. Pujara's pick, in other words, is not a form call; it is a bet on batting position and conditions.

Why Pujara sees a drawn series

On the series outcome, Pujara pointed to India's squad split across the five matches, with one group playing the first three ODIs and a different set of players taking over for the final two, ahead of a Test beginning November 19 in Wellington, CricTracker reports. That rotation, he argued, hands New Zealand a structural advantage because the hosts face a consistent lineup while India field two effectively separate sides.

"Two-all. In the first three matches, one team is playing, and then, in the last two matches, another Indian team is going to play."

— Cheteshwar Pujara, on JioStar

Pujara said he is still backing India in the first three matches, expects the last two to be a challenge, and expects a hard-fought series. He also factored in New Zealand's weather, noting that rain could wash out at least one game — the washout is what turns a five-match series into a 2-2 draw in his prediction. SportsTiger's report of the same JioStar comments carries the same prediction and the same reasoning on Kohli's No. 3 role.

What to watch

The series opens on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The first test of Pujara's reasoning comes immediately: whether Rohit's powerplay approach changes on New Zealand pitches, and whether Kohli gets the time at No. 3 to build the anchor innings Pujara describes. The second test comes late, when India's second squad group takes over for the final two matches. If Pujara is right on both counts, the series will be decided less by who is the better batter than by how India manage a split tour.
